precepts.text: Neither shall he go out of the sanctuary, for the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him; that is why they could not leave.
precepts.point: They were not to go out from the door of the tabernacle, for the anointing oil of the Lord was upon them. The anointing oil had already been put on them, so they could not leave the sanctuary.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
Aaron and his sons were told, “ye shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: for the anointing oil of the Lord is upon you.” The law of the priests says the same: “Neither shall he go out of the sanctuary, nor profane the sanctuary of his God; for the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him: I am the Lord.”

The anointing oil had already been put on Aaron and his sons, so they could not leave the sanctuary, not even for the death of Nadab and Abihu. The crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him; that is why they could not leave, “And they did according to the word of Moses.”

precepts.text: The words of chapter 19 went to all the congregation of the children of Israel, not to the priests only.
precepts.point: Christians will read verse 1 and say this chapter speaks only to the priests, so shaving the head and beard has nothing to do with them. But go back to chapter 19: the Lord spake there to all the children of Israel and said the exact same thing, round not the corners of your head, neither mar the corners of thy beard. The law given to the priests here was already the law of the whole nation; do not isolate the priests to escape the commandment.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
Christians read Leviticus 21:1 and say this chapter speaks only to the priests, so shaving the head and beard has nothing to do with them. Go back to chapter 19: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.”

The words of chapter 19 went to all the congregation of the children of Israel, not to the priests only. And in that chapter the Lord said the exact same thing about the head and the beard. The law given to the priests here was already the law of the whole nation.

precepts.text: Round not the corners of your head, neither mar the corners of thy beard; the same law binds every man of Israel.
precepts.point: Christians will read verse 1 and say this chapter speaks only to the priests, so shaving the head and beard has nothing to do with them. But go back to chapter 19: the Lord spake there to all the children of Israel and said the exact same thing, round not the corners of your head, neither mar the corners of thy beard. The law given to the priests here was already the law of the whole nation; do not isolate the priests to escape the commandment.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
To the priests: “They shall not make baldness upon their head, neither shall they shave off the corner of their beard.” To all the congregation of the children of Israel: “Ye shall not round the corners of your heads, neither shalt thou mar the corners of thy beard.”

It is the same law, and it binds every man of Israel. Do not isolate the priests to escape the commandment.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; under Christ there is room to repent and stand back up.
precepts.point: The daughter of any priest that profaned herself by playing the whore profaned her father and was burnt with fire. Under the law it was straight death, and we are all guilty of these things; this is why Christ had to come. Thank the Most High for the blood of Christ, that we can repent, correct ourselves, and keep moving, for a just man falleth and riseth up again.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
The priests were held to an even higher standard, and “the daughter of any priest, if she profane herself by playing the whore, she profaneth her father: she shall be burnt with fire.” Under the law it was straight death, and we are all guilty of these things; this is why Christ had to come.

“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” Thank the Most High for the blood of Christ, that we can repent, correct ourselves, and keep moving. Under Christ there is room to fall, repent and stand back up.

precepts.text: The veil of the temple was rent in twain when Christ died.
precepts.point: When Christ died the veil of the temple was rent and the priesthood was changed; the high priest now is Christ, for it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda. The sons of Levi no longer carry that office; Judah carries this work to the kingdom.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
The high priest, “upon whose head the anointing oil was poured”, could not go out of the sanctuary, “for the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him.” Under the old covenant his head was covered with the mitre.

When Christ died, “behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent.” The rending of the veil marks the change: the priesthood of Aaron’s sons and their sanctuary gave way, and the high priest now is Christ.

precepts.text: The priesthood being changed, there is a change also of the law; it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda.
precepts.point: When Christ died the veil of the temple was rent and the priesthood was changed; the high priest now is Christ, for it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda. The sons of Levi no longer carry that office; Judah carries this work to the kingdom.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
“For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.” The high priest of Leviticus 21 was of the sons of Aaron, of the tribe of Levi. But “he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar. For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

The high priest now is Christ, out of Juda. The sons of Levi no longer carry that office; Judah carries this work to the kingdom.

precepts.text: Whosoever of Aaron's seed hath any blemish, including him that hath his stones broken, shall not approach to offer the bread of his God.
precepts.point: This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“He that is wounded in the stones, or hath his privy member cut off, shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord.” This law repeats what was already given to the priests. Leviticus lists the blemishes that barred a man of Aaron's seed from approaching to offer the bread of his God: “a blind man, or a lame, or he that hath a flat nose, or any thing superfluous, Or a man that is brokenfooted, or brokenhanded, Or crookbackt, or a dwarf, or that hath a blemish in his eye, or be scurvy, or scabbed, or hath his stones broken”.

The same blemish is in both. “Whosoever he be of thy seed in their generations that hath any blemish, let him not approach to offer the bread of his God”, and among them is he that hath his stones broken; here he that is wounded in the stones shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. What was said of the priest's approach is said again of the congregation.
